answer: Agents earn voting weight from deposits locked for a fixed period, and each account’s weight is capped so splitting funds among many identities yields no extra influence. To change the registry, a proposal must pass a deposit-weighted quorum; challengers can submit evidence and slash deposits tied to proven fraud. A sybil attacker must therefore lock substantial capital and risk losing it, while waiting out the lockup. A jade ledger can mirror deposits across audits without letting any identity reach the zenith alone.
